etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English forgeten, forgiten, foryeten, forȝiten, from Old English forġietan (“to forget”) [influenced by Old Norse geta ("to get, to guess")], from Proto-West Germanic *fragetan (“to give up, forget”). Equivalent to for- +‎ get.

Cognate with :

quote.citation: 1593, Tho[mas] Nashe, Christs Teares Over Ierusalem. […], London:  […]  Iames Roberts, and are to be solde by Andrewe Wise, […], →OCLC, folio 60, verso:
quote.text: VVe (of all earthlings) are Gods vtmoſt ſubiects, the laſt (in a manner) that he bought to his obedience: ſhal we then forgette that vvee are any ſubiects of hys, becauſe (as amongſt his Angels) he is not viſibly conuerſant amongſt vs?

quote.citation: 1921 June, Margery Williams, “The Velveteen Rabbit: Or How Toys Become Real”, in Harper’s Bazar, volume LVI, number 6 (2504 overall), New York, N.Y.: International Magazine Company, →ISSN, →OCLC:
quote.text: For at least two hours the Boy loved him, and then Aunts and Uncles came to dinner, and there was a great rustling of tissue paper and unwrapping of parcels, and in the excitement of looking at all the new presents the Velveteen Rabbit was forgotten.

quote.citation: 1928, Lawrence R. Bourne, chapter 4, in Well Tackled!‎[1]:
quote.text: Technical terms like ferrite, perlite, graphite, and hardenite were bandied to and fro, and when Paget glibly brought out such a rare exotic as ferro-molybdenum, Benson forgot that he was a master ship-builder, […]

quote.citation: 1929, Robert Dean Frisbee, The Book of Puka-Puka, Eland, published 2019, page 35:
quote.text: Everybody, old and young, laughs uproariously at this and immediately forgets all about it.

In conditions of unlimited global-digital 'web-memory' (labelled by one critic a 'globital age'), social remembering and forgetting have become functions of algorithm-based search technologies that mine data from users  […]

quote.citation: 1905, Lord Dunsany [i.e., Edward Plunkett, 18th Baron of Dunsany], The Gods of Pegāna, London: [Charles] Elkin Mathews, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Pray, thou, therefore, to Slid, and forget not Slid, and it may be that Slid will not forget to send thee Death when most thou needest it.

definitions.definition: (transitive, loosely, informal) To not realize something (regardless of whether one has ever known it).
(slang) Euphemism for fuck, screw (a mild oath).
